the formation of benzene is the result of a complex interaction of the catalysts with both CH4 and CO.
, in the presence of CO, methane is activated on the catalyst surface to form CHx intermediates, and the CHx intermediates are converted into benzene and COx species by hydrogen transfer reactions.
, in the CH4-CO system, the formation of benzene is not a simple process, but a complex one, which involves the interaction of CH4 with CO and CO2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rh catalyst is more effective in benzene formation than Ru or Pd.
the reaction of CO with methane on the catalysts is not only a reaction for the formation of CO2, but also a reaction for the selective formation of benzene.
the formation of benzene from CH4-CO mixture is a complex reaction, which involves the formation and the decomposition of a number of intermediates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction of CO and CH4 over silica-supported Rh, Ru and Rh catalysts is a good route to produce benzene from CH4.
benzene formation is not the result of a simple disproportionation reaction of methane and carbon monoxide, and it is not an intermediate product of methane dehydrogenation.
